Subject: Private deploy — EU/APAC edge proxy handoff and residency guarantees

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Our procurement & security teams have a few open questions before we can complete the Private deployment procurement for Kronos Bank.

Topline asks:
- We need a concise description of how inbound traffic from EU users is terminated and how requests are routed to EU vs APAC private clusters (edge-proxy handoff). Where is customer data decrypted? 
- During a regional failure (EU zone outage) what is the failover behavior — do we allow cross-border processing to APAC? If so, how is that authorized/logged? 
- What are the egress IP ranges and what evidence can you provide for data residency (control-plane logs, HA handover audit trail)?

Can you share a network diagram and the minimal acceptance checklist your engineers need to validate residency constraints? We're aiming to sign by mid‑October and need this for our legal/security review.

Regards,
Eva Bergman
Head of Cloud Security
Kronos Bank

Subject: Re: Private deploy — EU/APAC edge proxy handoff and residency guarantees

Hi Eva — thanks for the clear list. I've attached a preliminary edge-handshake diagram and a draft acceptance checklist (see attachments).

Quick answers while the infra team pulls diagrams:
- Inbound termination happens at our customer-dedicated edge proxy in the region (EU). TLS is terminated at the customer-managed VPC peering endpoint or at a managed regional edge depending on deployment choice; decrypted payloads never leave the region unless the customer explicitly opts into cross-border failover.
- Failover: by default we perform "regional fail-open only after manual authorization" for data-residency-sensitive workloads. For customers who allow automatic failover, we require a signed policy in DocuSign and we emit a certified audit event for each request that crosses boundaries.
- Egress IPs: we can provide static egress ranges per deployment and a signed manifest. See attachment for the example ranges.

Propose a 45-minute network deep‑dive next Tue (Sep 29) with Vivek and Lauren to finalize acceptance criteria. Available windows: 09:00–11:00 or 15:00–17:00 CEST.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private deploy — technical notes on edge handoff and failover

Folks — adding technical constraints and proposed controls for the acceptance checklist.

Key points:
- Control-plane isolation: the control plane remains in a Redwood-managed VPC and establishes per-customer control-channel over an mTLS connection to the customer-managed control-proxy. Only control-plane metadata (no PII) crosses the managed boundary; we log every control handshake with timestamps and pod/node identifiers.
- Data-plane: model inference requests are served by region-affine worker pools. For "on-prem VPC" variants we support either (A) customer-hosted ingress + Redwood worker peering, or (B) managed regional edge that peers directly into customer VPC. In both cases we support IP allowlist and mandatory egress SNAT to a fixed range.
- Failover modes to propose:
  * Manual failover (default for residency-sensitive): runbook-triggered switchover; logs written to an immutable audit bucket in the customer's region.
  * Policy-based delayed failover: automatic after X minutes with pre-authorized signed policy; cross-border requests flagged and sampled for QA.
  * Hard failover (opt-in): immediate cross-region routing with full traffic mirroring for 1h post-switchover.
- Networking specifics: we recommend BGP peering for high-throughput customers and IPsec tunnels for regulated on‑prem links. We avoid hairpin NAT by terminating TLS at the customer edge when requested.
- Egress ranges: we'll provide CIDR ranges; we'll also publish a signed manifest and rotation schedule (monthly) and provide a signed snapshot at cutover for your procurement evidence.

I'll bring the diagram updates to Tue's call. /Vivek
From: pc-sec@kronosbank.se

Jasmine and Vivek,

Thanks — couple of clarifications from our security engineering checklist:
- We need the concrete egress IP list for the EU deployment and the proof artifact (signed manifest) prior to procurement.
- For manual failover we require an auditable approval flow (two SRE approvers) and retention of the approval artifacts for 7 years.
- Can you confirm whether the immutable audit bucket will be in our EU project (yes/no) and provide an example of the audit record format.
- Last: what is your RTO and RPO SLAs for the dedicated EU cluster under a zone-level outage?

If you can send these as separate artifacts (manifest, runbook, example records) we'll attach them to our legal package.

—Kronos Sec
